about: T3 workarounds of the workflow (PLAN M-decision 35). Every T3 upgrade runs `node <plugin>/bin/t3-workarounds.mjs check`; the code of each workaround carries the marker `T3-WORKAROUND(<id>)`.

workarounds.title: After /clear T3 keeps resuming the session it opened first; the hook links <cursor>.jsonl to the new session's transcript
depends_on: provider log <t3-home>/logs/provider/events.<thread, ':' -> '-'>.log with lines `[<ISO time>] ..."type":"query.open","options":{..."resume":"<session id>"`
T3 resumes the session id it opened with (claudeAgent resume cursor)
T3 sets T3CODE_THREAD_ID in the agent's environment
Claude Code appends to <session>.jsonl in place (Windows without Developer Mode: hard link instead of symlink, made by a detached process once the new transcript exists)
workarounds.remove_when: no machine runs T3 < 0.1.10; then remove the marked code (clearSession, t3_cursor) and this entry; realSessionDirs in t3-clear.mjs is not part of this workaround and stays
workarounds.verified: 2026-11-17, T3 0.1.10: pilot thread (code word, /clear, second word, interrupt) answered from the session after /clear; the provider log resumed the new session id (pingdotgg/t3code#35054 merged 2026-11-12). From 0.1.10 scripts/t3-clear.mjs leaves /clear alone (T3_CLEAR_FIXED).

workarounds.title: The hook cannot rename a thread; it reads the title via the T3 CLI and asks the agent to rename (P-036); topics start threads via the CLI
depends_on: `t3 thread show --json <missing thread>` exits non-zero naming it gone (0.1.10: "Thread <id> is no longer available."): scripts/thread-title.mjs THREAD_GONE; the limit of automatic topics leaves those holders out
`t3 thread start --json --title <title>` prints the new thread's id
workarounds.pilot: pilot: `topic create` from a thread holding a topic opens a new T3 thread titled by the topic
workarounds.remove_when: hooks can rename threads (no CLI dependency)
workarounds.verified: 2026-11-17, T3 0.1.10: `t3 thread start --title` opened a thread with that title, `thread show --json` printed title and archived, a missing thread answered "is no longer available" with exit 1. 2026-11-25, T3 0.1.12 (pilot): `topic create --new-thread` from a thread holding a topic opened a thread titled by the topic, `thread show --json` printed that title. 2026-11-27, T3 0.1.13 (pilot): the same result as on 0.1.12

workarounds.title: `t3 thread start` sets provider and model of a topic class (D-0021) but has no --effort; topic create/thread print a line to set the effort with t3_thread_configure
depends_on: t3_thread_configure takes threadId and modelSelection {instanceId, model, options: [{id: "effort", value}]}
workarounds.remove_when: `t3 thread start` takes --effort (the automatic check cli-effort then says REMOVE); upstream closed the request as not planned, so the workaround is expected to stay
workarounds.verified: 2026-11-17, T3 0.1.10: `t3 thread start --help` lists --title, --provider, --model, --worktree, --branch, --wait, --json and no --effort

workarounds.title: A send with fresh context queued behind a running turn opens a new Claude session and leaves the old one running; a background task of the old session still runs its turn there. UserPromptSubmit gives each session the turns the other session of the thread wrote since its last prompt

upstream.state: fix #38824 (T3 0.1.11) routes the operator's next prompt to the new session; the old session keeps running and writes its turns (verified on 0.1.12)

depends_on: T3 sets T3CODE_THREAD_ID in the agent's environment; every Claude session of one T3 thread shares its thread state
UserPromptSubmit input has session_id and transcript_path
Claude transcript lines carry type user/assistant, timestamp, isSidechain, isMeta and message.content
workarounds.pilot: pilot: in a thread start a background command that runs ~5 min and end the turn; send a message and, while its turn runs, queue one with fresh context (an idle thread with a background task refuses a fresh-context send from 0.1.12); after the command's notification send another: its context starts with "T3 session split" and holds the old session's reply to the notification
workarounds.remove_when: T3 ends the old session at a send with fresh context (none of its turns runs afterwards) or gives the new session those turns itself; then remove scripts/t3-stale-session.mjs, its call in hooks/user-prompt-submit.mjs, the test and this entry
workarounds.verified: 2026-11-19, T3 0.1.10: a replay of the 2026-11-18 incident transcripts gave the old session the operator's two prompts and the reply with options A/B (16 ms); a thread with one session reads no transcript. 2026-11-20: upstream closed #38764 as completed, the fix #38824 was merged 2026-11-19 and v0.1.11 (2026-11-20) contains its commit 66235c7; not verified on a running T3 0.1.11 yet. 2026-11-25, T3 0.1.12 (pilot, Bob's upgrade report): a fresh-context send queued behind a running turn opened a new session beside the old one with its background command; the command's notification ran a turn in the old session (it got the two prompts of the new session), the next prompt went to the new session (the upstream fix) and got the old session's reply. The workaround stays: without it the current session does not know what the old one wrote into the thread. 2026-11-27, T3 0.1.13 (pilot): the same result as on 0.1.12
